items.rationale: Control flow is the order of steps: in a workflow your code fixes it, in an agent the model decides the next step. Call count is tempting but a workflow can make many calls (a). Tools are tempting but workflows use tools too (b). Model size says nothing about who steers (d).

The code owns the control flow: the model's label only selects between paths the code already defined, so this is a workflow. Option b is tempting because a model output picks the branch, but the branches and their steps are fixed in code. Option c ties the label to tool use, which does not decide it. Option d counts model calls, which does not decide it either.

When the steps are known in advance, code can run them as a fixed workflow with fewer model calls, which is cheaper and more predictable. Option a is tempting because freedom sounds smarter, but nothing here needs the model to choose. Option b is tempting but both designs can call tools. Option c is tempting because agents adapt, but an agent spends extra calls deciding each next step.

Code routes by request type: the known booking path stays a fixed workflow, and only the open-ended troubleshooting path gets an agent loop. Option a pays for agent calls on bookings and gives up predictability. Option c cannot cover problems nobody listed ahead of time. Option d puts the agent where the steps are already known; tool calls do not make a task open-ended.

Finding a machine that fits has no fixed path: how many machines to look at and which tools to use are unknown in advance, so the model must choose each next step. Option a has several steps but the same ones every time. Option b is a fixed manual lookup. Option d is a fixed record lookup. A workflow handles all three.

A fixed path is set in code, so behavior is predictable and easy to test and explain. Option b is tempting but reverses the two: adapting to the unplanned is what an agent does. Option c is tempting because code runs the steps, but a workflow still calls the model at its steps. Option d assumes fixed means more accurate, but a fixed path cannot adapt to open-ended work.
